programs.title: Global Exchange Seminar (Tokyo)
programs.desc: An intensive 4-week cultural immersion and technical research seminar hosted in collaboration with university partners in Shinjuku, Tokyo.
programs.eligibility: Enrolled university students or recent graduates (within 2 years). Basic English proficiency. Open to all majors.

programs.title: Cross-Cultural Communications (Munich)
programs.desc: Explores multinational operations and communication behaviors within European business markets, hosted in Munich, Germany.
programs.eligibility: Senior undergraduates, graduates, or young corporate recruits. IELTS 6.5 or equivalent recommended.

programs.title: Executive Corporate Governance
programs.desc: Geared towards managers and governance officers looking to implement compliance framework designs and sustainable ESG policies.
programs.eligibility: Minimum 3 years of executive or managerial experience. Corporate sponsorship accepted.

programs.title: Resilient Leadership Architecture
programs.desc: Equips teams with strategic risk assessment models, crisis management pathways, and communication protocols during organizational pivots.
programs.eligibility: Project managers, department leads, and senior team members.

programs.title: Civic Youth Fellowship
programs.desc: A selective 6-month incubator backing community project proposals with seed metrics, leadership resources, and policy coaching.
programs.eligibility: Ages 18 to 30. Active member of a community group or local nonprofit. A project proposal brief is required.

programs.title: Social Enterprise Accelerator
programs.desc: Helps early-stage social founders refine business plans, build pitch decks, and raise operational capital.
programs.eligibility: Founders of registered social businesses, B-corps, or non-profits less than 2 years old.
benefits: Pitch deck feedback from impact VCs

historyMilestones.title: UPG Conference at ASCM
historyMilestones.desc: The Unreached People Groups (UPG) conference at the Asian Seminary of Christian Ministries (ASCM) became the seedbed for MERU. Rev. Dr. Roland Vaughan, coordinator of Church of God World Missions (COGWM) UPG Missions, served as keynote speaker, inspiring partnerships that later shaped MERU.

historyMilestones.title: Birth of partnerships
historyMilestones.desc: The conference fostered collaborations among leaders and missionaries who were instrumental in developing MERU’s vision and strategies.

historyMilestones.title: Doctor of ministry research project
historyMilestones.desc: Dr. George Pappachen, an ASCM D.Min. graduate, conducted research on Christian Missions for the Unreached (CMU) among the Agta people of Palanan, Isabela, Philippines. His focus on 'gospel inculturation' documented best practices and laid the foundation for innovative UPG mission strategies.

historyMilestones.title: Formation of MERU Global Team
historyMilestones.desc: Emerging from the mission's atmosphere of innovation and partnership, MERU Global Team was established as a new addition to organizations serving UPG missions worldwide. It stands as a testimony to the call of Christ to birthing ministries that connect people to the Great Commission.

historyMilestones.title: Global Expansion
historyMilestones.desc: Today, MERU has spread to nations across the world, launching training programs, hosting conferences, and building bridges between generations and cultures. Through these initiatives, MERU continues to gather people for the Great Commission, empowering Christians to reach the unreached with the Gospel.
